subject: Quarter close: performance signals, closure notes & lessons learned
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-12-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quarter close: performance signals, closure notes & lessons learned

Team —

Attached is the working scoring workbook for Q4 (tabbed by org area) and the draft narrative (qbr-narrative-draft-v3.pdf). Aim is to lock scores + narrative excerpts by end of day tomorrow so we can circulate to exec comms on Wednesday morning. High-level asks:

- Please review your org area tab in the spreadsheet and add any missing evidence links under the "evidence" column. Use the shorthand score scale we agreed on (0/0.5/1.0) and add a one-line justification.
- For the narrative PDF, I pulled three signal lines per priority: one win, one problem, one action. If you have a different framing, highlight the paragraph and add a comment in Drive.
- Highlight any hard escalations or ask-for-help items (budget, headcount, infra) with clear owners and required dates — I will pull these into the QBR decision slide.

A few cross-org notes from my review:
- Serving Runtime (Engineering): strong latency and cost improvements; still seeing customer regressions on long-context queries (see redwood/telemetry link in sheet).
- Dedicated/Dedicated Sales ops: pipeline conversion for Reserved Capacity underperformed target vs. motion (down 18% QoQ) — Marcus, please add customer evidence.
- Observability + Rollouts: good progress on tracing hooks; we need an ask on extended retention for one pilot customer (BrightPath).

Timeline: lock scores by 2026-12-21 17:00 PT, narrative edits by 2026-12-22 09:00 PT. I will synthesize and produce the final one-pager for QBR slides on 12/22 afternoon.

Attachments (stubs): 2026Q4_goal-scoring-and-evidence.xlsx (xlsx), qbr-narrative-draft-v3.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — brief replies ok when you’ve updated.

Rachel Kim
Head of Strategy & Insights
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quarter close: performance signals, closure notes & lessons learned

Rachel — thanks for the packet, I skimmed the Serving Runtime tab and left three quick notes in the sheet. Main points:

- I bumped the "latency SLO improvements" score to 1.0; we hit the internal benchmark for p99 on shorter sequences and that’s driven a noticeable reduction in customer errors. Evidence: PR #4872 and telemetry summary (link in sheet).
- Long-context regressions: agree with the observation. We have a mitigant (kv-cache tuning) scheduled for next sprint but it’s not deployed broadly — provisional score 0.5 until rollout is complete.
- Chore alignment: I flagged two backlog items that were deprioritized and should be re-raised for the next sprint planning.

I also added a one-line narrative suggestion: flip the second signal to call out the cost-per-token gains as a concrete business impact (saves X% on typical inference workloads) rather than a purely engineering metric.

Laura
VP Product Operations

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quarter close: performance signals, closure notes & lessons learned

Adding my items — updated the Reserved Capacity tab and attached two customer examples in the sheet: Acme Corp (declined conversion, cited performance SLA mismatch) and BrightPath (near-term upsell discussion, ask for extended observability retention).

Notes:
- Reserved Capacity conversion: score 0.5. We had a couple of close-won but net was below plan; primary blocker was pricing headroom + initial throughput not matching the customer's long-tail queries. Evidence: Acme email thread (referenced in sheet) and demo logs (link).
- Deal support required: request $25k pilot credit approval for Acme to run a full workload test next quarter; without pilot they push to a competitor.

Attachments referenced: demo-logs-acme-20261201.zip (attachment stub referenced in sheet)

Marcus
Head of Sales, Dedicated Capacity

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-21T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quarter close: performance signals, closure notes & lessons learned

Folks — great synth so far. Two operational asks from my side before we finalize:

1) Headcount ask: the Observability roadmap needs an additional 0.5 FTE (contractor) for Q1 to complete the extended tracing retention pilot. If we can approve a $40k budget line, we can deliver by end of Jan.

2) Exec narrative: we should be explicit about our "graceful degradation" story — call out fallback policies and percentage of traffic successfully served by fallback in the narrative (I added numbers in the brief). This helps counterbalance the long-context regression item when presenting to execs.

I reviewed the BrightPath ask — approved to include in the QBR decision slide as "pilot ask" with Marcus as owner. On Acme: ok to consider a one-time pilot credit but let's gate by a short-run performance test and a signed MoU (Marcus, could you push that to legal?).

Vivek
Director, Platform Reliability

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-12-21T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quarter close: performance signals, closure notes & lessons learned

Thanks all — I incorporated Laura's framing change and Marcus/Vivek's asks into the sheet and the narrative. Quick decisions recorded:

- Serving Runtime: final score 0.75 (evidence links in spreadsheet). Narrative now highlights cost-per-token wins + fallback policy stats (Vivek numbers inserted).
- Reserved Capacity: final score 0.5. Marcus to draft MoU for Acme; finance to confirm pilot-credit approval process (I added a finance action item).
- Observability retention pilot: approve contractor + $40k budget line as a Q1 decision. Marcus to track pilot as a separate line in the QBR slide.

Next steps: I’ll produce the one-page QBR summary and a slide with decision items and owners by EOD 12/22. Please review the updated files in Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/QBR-2026-Q4 — I will lock the narrative by 12/22 15:00 PT.

If there are no objections, I’ll forward the finalized deck to exec comms on 12/23 morning.

Rachel
Head of Strategy & Insights
Redwood Inference
